\section[l'imputato]{l'imputato — the defendant, the accused}

\label{lesson:IT-C392-imputato}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the criminal complaint, then the Italian for the corruption.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'imputato}
\textbf{l'imputato} — \textquotedblleft{}the defendant, the accused\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'imputato dice di essere innocente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The defendant says he is innocent.}
\end{quote}

A woman is \emph{l'imputata}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{imputato} is the past participle of \emph{imputare} \textquotedblleft{}to charge with\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{imputāre} \textquotedblleft{}to reckon in, to charge to\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{putāre} \textquotedblleft{}to reckon\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'imputato}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'imputato}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'imputato}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the criminal complaint, then the Italian for the corruption, then say \emph{l'imputato} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does l'imputato mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The defendant, the accused\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la difesa]{la difesa — the defence}

\label{lesson:IT-C392-difesa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the corruption, then the Italian for the defendant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la difesa}
\textbf{la difesa} — \textquotedblleft{}the defence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'avvocato della difesa parla per ultimo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The defence lawyer speaks last.}
\end{quote}

In sport, the defence too. \emph{Per legittima difesa} — in self-defence.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{difesa} is inherited from Late Latin \emph{dēfēnsa} \textquotedblleft{}a defending\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{dēfendere} \textquotedblleft{}to ward off, to defend\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la difesa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la difesa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the corruption, then the Italian for the defendant, then say \emph{la difesa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[la sentenza]{la sentenza — the verdict, the ruling}

\label{lesson:IT-C392-sentenza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the defendant, then the Italian for the defence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la sentenza}
\textbf{la sentenza} — \textquotedblleft{}the verdict, the ruling\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La sentenza arriva la settimana prossima.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The verdict comes next week.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Sputare sentenze} — to lay down the law, to pontificate.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sentenza} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{sententia} \textquotedblleft{}an opinion, a judgement, a maxim\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{sentīre} \textquotedblleft{}to feel, to think\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la condanna]{la condanna — the conviction, the sentence}

\label{lesson:IT-C392-condanna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the defence, then the Italian for the verdict.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la condanna}
\textbf{la condanna} — \textquotedblleft{}the conviction, the sentence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La condanna è di due anni.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The sentence is two years.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{condannare}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{condanna} is built on \emph{condannare} \textquotedblleft{}to sentence\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{condemnāre} \textquotedblleft{}to condemn\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{damnāre}, from \emph{damnum} \textquotedblleft{}loss, penalty\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la pena]{la pena — the penalty, the punishment; the pity}

\label{lesson:IT-C392-pena}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the verdict, then the Italian for the conviction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la pena}
\textbf{la pena} — \textquotedblleft{}the penalty, the punishment; the pity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Per questo reato la pena è molto alta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{For this crime the penalty is very high.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Vale la pena} — it is worth it. \emph{Mi fa pena} — I feel sorry for him.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pena} is inherited from Latin \emph{poena} \textquotedblleft{}penalty, punishment\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), an early borrowing from Greek \emph{poin\'{\={e}}} \textquotedblleft{}blood money, a fine\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
